source: schema/changelog-24.55.0-hrms-role-set.xml, plus 24.52.0 and 24.56.0 for the self-service rung. Permission counts verified against the live role grants.
note: Seven rungs, each the smallest set that lets somebody finish their own job. Nothing stops one person holding more than one role — that is a decision for whoever assigns them.

roles.name: HRMS_EMPLOYEE_SELF
roles.what: The login an employee is handed for their own record. Reaches My HR and nothing else.
can: Their own payslips, attendance, leave balance and details, through /hrms/me
cannot: See any other employee, anywhere in the module

Apply for leave or submit a claim through the main screens — those endpoints are organisation-wide, so an employee holding them would see every colleague's leave and every colleague's claims. They are deliberately withheld.
roles.watch: The role is called HRMS_EMPLOYEE_SELF, not EMPLOYEE. A role named plainly EMPLOYEE collided with an existing one, and every workforce login issued silently received all 53 permissions instead of one.

roles.name: ATTENDANCE_TAKER
roles.what: Marks the daily attendance of the branch or office they are posted to.
can: See the employee list — the marking screen is a list of employees
View and mark attendance
See their own record, because whoever marks the roster is also on it

roles.name: BRANCH_SUPERVISOR
roles.what: Runs a branch day to day: attendance, leave, expense claims and penalties for their own people.
can: Everything the attendance taker can
Approve leave
Raise a penalty
Pass an expense claim
Read departments, advances, contract workers and performance
cannot: Correct attendance on a day payroll has already consumed — that changes a figure somebody has been paid against, so it is an HR_ADMIN action

roles.name: HR_MANAGER
roles.what: Runs the module: employee master, wage master, statutory returns and payroll processing.
can: Create and edit employees
Manage departments, designations, grades and employment types
View salary and raise a pay revision
Process the monthly payroll run
Approve leave and expense claims, raise penalties and advances
Manage contract workers
Generate EPF, ESIC and Form-II returns
cannot: Approve a payroll run at either level — processing and approving must be two different acts, and this is the processing one
Sign the pay revision it raised, for the same reason
Delete an employee, or see unmasked identity numbers

roles.name: HR_ADMIN
roles.what: First signature: approves payroll runs and pay revisions at level 1, and corrects locked attendance.
can: Everything HR_MANAGER can
Approve a payroll run at L1, and a pay revision at L1
Override attendance on a locked day
Delete an employee record
See unmasked identity numbers (UAN, ESIC, PAN, Aadhaar)
Approve penalties, rate performance, read the payroll journal
Mark a released run paid, or cancel one
cannot: Release a run — that is the second signature, and it belongs to HR_HEAD

roles.name: HR_HEAD
roles.what: Second signature: releases payroll runs and pay revisions at level 2.
can: Approve a payroll run at L2, and a pay revision at L2 — the approvals that release either
Read the figures, the register behind them and the ledger they post to
Approve leave, expense claims and penalties
See unmasked identity numbers
cannot: Process payroll — this role cannot compute the run it releases
Create or edit employees, or touch the masters

roles.name: HEAD_OFFICE
roles.what: Head office and accounts: payroll settings, the wage master and the payroll ledger.
can: Manage payroll settings — PF and ESIC rates, professional tax, the duty base
Manage the wage master every employee's basic is looked up in
Manage designations, grades and employment types
Read widely across the module, because a rate cannot be set sensibly without seeing what it does
cannot: Sign at either level. Somebody who both sets the rates and releases the run should be given HR_HEAD as well, deliberately, rather than this role quietly including it.

platform.what: The platform administrators, who already administer every other module. They hold the whole vocabulary including both signatures — somebody has to be able to unstick a tenant that has assigned its roles badly.

rules.title: Two signatures, and they are different roles
rules.body: A payroll run and a pay revision both need L1 then L2. That is why the top of the ladder is split: HR_MANAGER computes, HR_ADMIN signs first, HR_HEAD signs second. A run one person can compute, approve and release is not controlled at all.

rules.title: But there is no different-person rule
rules.body: Nothing stops one login holding HR_ADMIN and HR_HEAD and clearing both levels. The run records who signed each level, so the trail shows when they were the same person. If you want two people, assign two people.

rules.title: A penalty needs only one approver
rules.body: hrms:penalty:approve is the whole requirement. Do not wait for a second signature — the two-person rule belongs to payments in the Accounting module, not here.
